candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

candidates.cover_letter:
Halie Fox
310-422-3163 | haliefox8@gmail.com
Re: MSW Practicum Placement – January 2027
Dear Hiring and Clinical Education Team,
I am writing to express my interest in exploring a Master of Social Work (MSW) practicum placement with your organizations in Davie, Florida, specifically Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am currently pursuing my MSW and am seeking a practicum opportunity beginning in January 2027, as I will be relocating to the Fort Lauderdale area.
My professional and academic experiences have strengthened my passion for providing compassionate, client-centered support to individuals navigating complex life circumstances. Through my work as a Direct Services Coordinator with Housing Matters, I provided trauma-informed support to individuals experiencing homelessness, conducted basic needs assessments, and connected clients with housing, healthcare, and community resources. I have also worked with adults with disabilities in an individualized, strengths-based capacity, supporting independence, self-advocacy, and community engagement.
Currently, I am gaining additional clinical experience through my MSW internship at Washington Area Clinical Center, where I assist with treatment planning, quality assurance calls, patient follow-ups, clinical documentation, and observe intake assessments and patient-provider interactions. These experiences have expanded my interest in clinical social work and have motivated me to continue developing my skills in assessment, therapeutic engagement, and interdisciplinary care.
I am particularly interested in the opportunity to gain experience in both adolescent mental health and substance use recovery settings. I would welcome the opportunity to learn from the clinical teams at either Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center and contribute to the meaningful work being done to support individuals and families. I value approaches grounded in empathy, collaboration, cultural humility, and an understanding of the unique experiences and strengths each client brings to the therapeutic process.
As I prepare for my relocation to South Florida, I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss potential January practicum openings, supervision availability, and the application process for either Davie location. I would be happy to provide additional information about my university's practicum requirements and coordinate with your team regarding placement expectations.
Thank you for your time and consideration,
Halie Fox

candidates.cover_letter:
JUAN CORDOBA, MBA
Miami, Florida
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in leadership, management, and operational opportunities within your organization. With over 12 years of progressive professional experience, a Master of Business Administration (MBA), and a Bachelor of Science in Health Care Administration, both earned Summa Cum Laude, I bring a strong combination of business knowledge, operational expertise, and hands-on leadership experience.
Throughout my career, I have held positions of increasing responsibility, including Staff Coordinator, Director of Social Services, Executive Director, Facility Administrator, and most recently, Regional Administrator. These roles have allowed me to develop extensive experience overseeing daily operations, managing multidisciplinary teams, improving organizational performance, implementing policies and procedures, and maintaining high standards of operational efficiency and accountability.
In my most recent position as Regional Administrator at Balanced Wellbeing, I oversaw healthcare service operations across multiple facilities throughout South Florida. My responsibilities included monitoring operational performance, managing provider productivity, coordinating staffing and onboarding, improving workflows, supporting regulatory compliance, and maintaining strong relationships with facility administrators and executive leadership.
One of my key strengths is my ability to identify operational challenges, develop effective solutions, and implement improvements that support organizational goals. I have managed competing priorities across multiple locations while maintaining a strong focus on employee performance, customer satisfaction, quality assurance, and operational consistency.
Although my professional background has primarily been in healthcare administration, my leadership experience extends beyond the healthcare setting. I possess transferable skills in business operations, strategic planning, team development, financial oversight, performance management, regulatory compliance, and organizational improvement. I am confident in my ability to apply these skills across a wide range of industries.
My leadership philosophy is built on accountability, collaboration, professionalism, and continuous improvement. I believe successful organizations depend on strong leadership, clear communication, efficient processes, and employees who feel supported and empowered to perform at their best.
I am interested in joining an organization where I can contribute my experience, embrace new challenges, and continue growing professionally while making a meaningful impact. I am adaptable, results-oriented, and committed to operational excellence and long-term organizational success.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, professional experience, and leadership capabilities can contribute to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Juan Cordoba, MBA

Dear Hiring Manager,

Sincerely,

Louisha Freeman, BS

Sincerely,

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,
I am writing to express my interest in the Adolescent Mental Health Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern with an MSW from Florida Atlantic University, I am dedicated to working alongside vulnerable children and families, and I would welcome the chance to bring my hands-on clinical experience and my commitment to growth to your team.
In my current role as Family Advocate / Clinical Case Manager at CityHouse, I deliver crisis intervention, de-escalation, and stabilization services, conduct comprehensive psychosocial and needs assessments with resident families, and provide counseling to children and families using evidence-based, trauma-informed interventions. I develop individualized treatment plans with measurable goals in collaboration with clients and the clinical team, then monitor progress and adjust plans as needs change. I also assisted in developing a children's therapeutic service program and an intentional therapeutic room across two campuses, a space designed so children feel safe and supported.
My MSW internship at CityHouse deepened my work with children and their caregivers. I created and facilitated an 8-week social-emotional learning group for children ages 8-12, and I advocated for IEP and educational needs for elementary-aged children, supporting mothers at parent-teacher conferences. Earlier, as a BSW intern and Behavioral Technician at Aces for Autism, I provided 1:1 applied behavior analysis sessions for children, including children with autism spectrum disorder, and completed clinical documentation. Together, these experiences taught me to meet each family where they are and build on their strengths.
What draws me to social work is the opportunity to walk alongside children and families through difficult moments and help them recognize their own strengths. I am currently accruing clinical hours toward LCSW licensure in Florida, and I am committed to ongoing growth through supervision, training, and hands-on practice.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy, and I can be reached at 845-600-5746 or accurson02@yahoo.com.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I am a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults in educational, recreational, and community-based settings.

My clinical experience includes providing individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health and working with adolescents and young adults at Family First and New Directions for Young Adults. I have developed and facilitated experiential therapeutic groups incorporating DBT skills, interpersonal effectiveness, emotional regulation, mindfulness, creative expression, and adventure-based activities. My approach integrates Adlerian theory, CBT, DBT, Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions, with a strong emphasis on therapeutic relationships, belonging, encouragement, and personal growth.

Prior to entering the counseling profession, I spent more than 15 years in youth engagement, Jewish education, summer camps, and challenge course programming. These experiences strengthened my ability to build rapport with adolescents, facilitate meaningful group experiences, navigate challenging interpersonal dynamics, and create supportive environments that encourage self-discovery.

I also serve as an adjunct instructor at Lynn University and remain actively engaged in the therapeutic adventure and experiential education community. In fact, I am currently attending our annual international conference in Estes Park, Colorado, where I continue to connect with fellow professionals, exchange ideas, and explore innovative approaches to experiential learning and therapeutic practice. I bring a creative, collaborative, strengths-based approach to counseling and a passion for helping young people develop the skills, confidence, and connections necessary to thrive.

As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am deeply passionate about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator. Professionally, I bring over six years of experience in the mental health field. Personally, I bring nearly 20 years of life experiences shaped by supporting family members and friends throughout their mental health journeys. These experiences have continually taught me the importance of understanding others beyond their immediate circumstances. Patience, calmness, and empathy are qualities that come naturally to me. Combined with my warm and engaging personality, they allow me to create meaningful connections and provide reassurance, even through a simple phone conversation.

During my time at Woodland Springs Behavioral Health, I began my career as a Behavioral Health Technician (BHT) working mainly on the Adolescent units,before advancing into an Intake Coordinator position. This transition allowed me to experience two equally important aspects of patient care: building relationships with patients during treatment and supporting individuals and families as they entered or completed the admissions process. Witnessing patients arrive during some of their most vulnerable moments and later recognizing their progress strengthened my appreciation for the trust placed in behavioral health professionals.

My experience has also taught me that compassion is especially important when working with individuals who may be frightened, frustrated, or resistant to treatment. I understand that anger and resistance can sometimes mask fear, uncertainty, or emotional distress. Rather than focusing solely on someone’s immediate reaction, I strive to understand the person behind the behavior, establish trust, and create an environment where individuals feel safe enough to communicate openly. I recognize that seeking treatment can be intimidating, and I believe meaningful support begins with making people feel heard rather than judged.

As an Intake Coordinator, I managed incoming admissions calls, conducted patient intake assessments, verified insurance coverage and benefits, and coordinated admissions with nurses, physicians, and other healthcare professionals. I also maintained accurate patient records and guided families through the admissions process. These responsibilities strengthened my ability to navigate sensitive situations with professionalism, organization, empathy, and attention to detail.

I understand how overwhelming seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be for families, particularly when their children are involved. My professional background, combined with my personal understanding of mental health challenges, has prepared me to approach these conversations with compassion, patience, and reassurance.

For me, working in mental health is more than a profession; it is an extension of who I am. I would be honored to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine care for others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Desiree Brown

candidates.cover_letter:
Emilia Huaman
San Diego, California

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. What immediately caught my attention about this opportunity was not only the work itself, but the mission behind it. Throughout my professional experience, I have always been drawn to work that allows me to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young people and families, especially those navigating difficult circumstances.

For over five years, I have worked in nonprofit and community-based settings, focusing on youth development, emotional support, and helping vulnerable communities access the resources they need. My experience has taught me that sometimes the most important part of someone’s journey is simply having the right person listen, understand their situation, and help them take the next step.

One of the experiences that has shaped me the most was founding Warmikuna, a nonprofit initiative in Peru dedicated to supporting adolescent mothers who were survivors of sexual abuse. Building this organization from the ground up required more than leadership. It required patience, empathy, resourcefulness, collaboration, and a genuine commitment to the people we served. I worked alongside mental health professionals, legal advocates, volunteers, and community organizations to help young women access support and opportunities to rebuild their lives.

More recently, as a Youth Program Coordinator at Casa Familiar in San Diego, I have continued working closely with adolescents, families, and community partners. My responsibilities have included program coordination, administrative tasks, outreach, communication, and connecting families with available resources. I have also gained experience navigating Medi-Cal and health insurance-related processes, which has strengthened my understanding of how important access to services can be for families.

I understand that admissions is often the first point of contact for someone seeking help. I would approach that responsibility with patience, professionalism, discretion, and compassion. I am also comfortable with administrative responsibilities, phone communication, digital tools, and learning new systems. While I have not yet worked with Kipu, I am very willing to learn and confident in my ability to adapt quickly.

I am currently continuing my education at San Diego Miramar College, pursuing Administration of Justice, and was honored to earn a place on the Dean’s List with a 4.0 GPA. I see my education and professional experience as complementary parts of the same goal: continuing to grow while contributing to work that has a positive impact on people’s lives.

I would be genuinely excited to bring my experience, bilingual communication skills, and commitment to youth advocacy to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your admissions team.

Warm regards,

Emilia Huaman

Admissions Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

RE: Application for Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Admissions Team,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, an active Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification, and over three years of experience supporting individuals, families, and adults with disabilities—including remote client support and multi-platform record tracking—I am eager to be a compassionate, dependable first point of contact for callers seeking care.

When individuals or families reach out for mental health or substance use support, clarity, patience, and consistent follow-through make all the difference. During my time at Pride Industries, I supported participants—including adults with disabilities—and their families across both remote and in-person settings, guiding them through structured programs, explaining next steps clearly, and resolving roadblocks to help achieve a 91% retention rate. Working remotely, I managed my own workflow and participated in regular virtual meetings with managers and support teams to coordinate follow-ups, review progress, and keep cases moving forward.

Accuracy and confidentiality are also central to how I work. Across Pride Industries and my earlier Business Systems & Operations Support internship at Rebuilding Together San Diego, I tracked inquiries, verified records, and maintained structured documentation across more than 11 enterprise platforms—building strong habits around organized pipeline tracking, thorough recordkeeping, and accountable follow-through.

I am excited about the opportunity to bring empathy, steady communication, and disciplined organization to your admissions team in a fully remote role. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

Robert Yelland

 As an as an Operations Manager with Care Center, I developed strong organizational, communication, and administrative skills. What draws me most to this opportunity is the ability to combine my professional strengths with work that has a meaningful impact on people's lives. I understand that admissions is more than answering calls and scheduling appointments. It is often the first opportunity to offer reassurance, build trust, and help someone take an important step toward healing.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my compassion, reliability, and dedication to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to helping others align with your mission.

Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Adolescent Admissions Coordinator position. With a Doctorate in Clinical Psychology (PsyD), seven years of experience as a therapist, and 14 years of experience in substance use disorder treatment, I bring a strong clinical background and a comprehensive understanding of the emotional, behavioral, and developmental needs of adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have gained extensive experience in clinical assessments, crisis intervention, diagnostic formulation, treatment planning, case management, and coordination of behavioral health services. My experience working with individuals presenting with mental health concerns, substance use disorders, and co-occurring conditions has strengthened my ability to identify clinical needs, assess risk, and facilitate access to appropriate levels of care.

I understand that the admissions process is often the first point of contact for families navigating challenging and emotionally overwhelming circumstances. My clinical training and interpersonal skills allow me to approach these conversations with compassion, professionalism, and sensitivity while gathering essential information and helping families understand their treatment options. I am also experienced in collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and managing confidential information in accordance with ethical and regulatory standards.

As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I am committed to reducing barriers to treatment and providing culturally responsive support to adolescents and their families. My ability to establish rapport, communicate complex clinical information, and navigate sensitive situations would allow me to contribute effectively to your admissions team.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it allows me to combine my clinical expertise with my passion for connecting individuals and families to meaningful treatment and recovery services. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, organizational skills, and commitment to quality patient care to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and professional experience align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Maria Velazquez, PsyD

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and extensive professional experience supporting adolescents and vulnerable populations, I believe my background aligns well with your organization’s mission. Throughout my career, I have worked in crisis intervention, transitional housing, and direct support services, where I developed strong skills in communication, conflict resolution, documentation, and providing compassionate care. My experience has allowed me to understand the importance of creating a safe and supportive environment for individuals experiencing emotional, behavioral, and personal challenges. I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its commitment to helping teenagers navigate mental health challenges while encouraging personal growth and emotional well-being.
During my time at Huckleberry House, I served as a Lead Crisis Intervention Specialist, where I supported adolescents experiencing crisis situations and assisted with maintaining a safe and structured environment. My responsibilities included crisis de-escalation, client intake, maintaining confidential documentation, and communicating with team members to ensure individuals received appropriate support. Additionally, my experience working in transitional housing strengthened my ability to assist vulnerable individuals with navigating difficult circumstances while maintaining professionalism, patience, and empathy. Through my work with Sevita, I further developed my ability to provide individualized support to people with disabilities while promoting independence and overall well-being. These experiences have strengthened my ability to remain calm under pressure, establish trusting relationships, and approach challenging situations with understanding rather than judgment.
I believe adolescents deserve to be heard, respected, and supported, especially during some of the most challenging stages of their development. My educational background in psychology, combined with my professional experience and leadership skills, has prepared me to contribute positively to an organization dedicated to improving the lives of young people. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my compassion, organizational abilities, and commitment to quality care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience can contribute to your team and the individuals you serve.
Thank you, Keaisia Herring

November 17, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I was genuinely drawn to this opportunity because it combines two things I value in my work: helping people and making what can sometimes be an overwhelming experience feel a little easier. I understand that someone reaching out to an admissions team may be navigating a difficult situation, whether they are seeking help for themselves or trying to find support for their child. I would take that responsibility seriously and approach every conversation with patience, compassion, and without judgment.

My background includes over two years of customer service experience in high-volume contact center environments, including remote phone and chat support, digital banking, and healthcare. In my previous role as a Certified Pharmacy Technician with Rite Aid, I assisted patients with insurance claims, billing concerns, prescription needs, and communication with healthcare providers while maintaining strict confidentiality and attention to detail. In my current role with U.S. Bank, I work with customers on sensitive account matters, navigate multiple systems, troubleshoot concerns, and make sure they receive accurate information and solutions. These experiences have taught me how to listen carefully, ask the right questions, explain information clearly, and follow through rather than leave someone feeling like they have to figure things out on their own.

What stood out to me about Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center is the emphasis on treating people as individuals and supporting not only the person seeking care, but their families as well. I appreciate that your programs recognize how important it is for people to feel welcomed, understood, and supported from the very first interaction. I would love to be part of that first step, helping callers understand their options, navigating insurance questions, coordinating next steps, and making the admissions process feel as comfortable and straightforward as possible.

I am organized, dependable, comfortable working independently in a remote environment, and quick to learn new systems and processes. Most importantly, I genuinely care about the experience people have when they reach out for help. I would be excited to bring my healthcare and customer service background, strong communication skills, and compassionate approach to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you and learn more about how I could contribute to your admissions team.

Warm regards,

Morgan Rados

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions and Intake Coordinator position. With over five years of experience in customer service and client support, a bachelor's degree in human services/counseling, and a Case Management certification, I feel this opportunity would be a great fit for both my professional experience and my passion for helping others.

During my time with Senture LLC and General Dynamics Information Technology, I worked fully remotely, assisting individuals over the phone, answering questions, resolving concerns, and helping callers navigate different systems and services. Working from home has taught me the importance of staying organized, managing my time, and being dependable without someone constantly overseeing my work. I am comfortable handling a high volume of calls, documenting information accurately, following up on concerns, and making sure people receive the assistance they need.

My background in Human Services/Counseling is one of the main reasons this position interests me. I have always enjoyed working with people and helping them find the right resources, especially when they may be going through a difficult time. I understand that reaching out for behavioral health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming for individuals and their families. I believe having someone on the other end of the phone who is patient, understanding, and willing to listen can make a real difference.

While my previous positions have focused primarily on customer service and client assistance rather than direct behavioral health admissions, I have experience handling sensitive information, maintaining detailed records, and communicating with individuals from different backgrounds. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and procedures, including admissions software, insurance verification processes, and patient intake requirements.

What interests me most about this opportunity is the chance to put my education and professional experience to work in a field that is meaningful to me. I am looking for a position where I can continue growing professionally while making a positive difference in people's lives. I would be grateful for the opportunity to become part of a team that helps individuals and families take important steps toward getting the care they need.

Thank you for taking the time to review my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about the position and how my experience and skills could benefit your team.

Sincerely,

Reba Johnson-Lewis

I also understand that the admissions coordinator plays an important role in connecting families with the resources and care they need during a critical time in their lives.

What interests me most about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to make a difference by helping young people access the support and treatment they deserve. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in an opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am passionate about working with adolescents and individuals who may be facing challenges related to substance use, mental health, behavior, and life circumstances. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my professional experience, education, and commitment to the helping professions in an environment focused on supporting young people and their overall wellness.

My professional background in Property Management has provided me with extensive experience working directly with individuals from diverse backgrounds, managing sensitive situations, resolving conflicts, maintaining accurate documentation, communicating effectively, and enforcing policies while treating residents with professionalism and respect. Property management has taught me the importance of patience, active listening, problem-solving, accountability, and building positive relationships—skills that I believe transfer strongly into a behavioral health and adolescent support setting.

Alongside my professional experience, I am pursuing my long-term career goal of becoming a Substance Abuse Counselor. Through my education at the College of the Siskiyous, I have completed coursework in Case Management, Relapse Prevention, Introduction to Psychology, Social Problems, Chemical Dependency Law, and Ethics of Health Professions. These courses have strengthened my understanding of substance use, recovery, behavioral health, ethical responsibilities, case management, and the social factors that can influence an individual’s well-being and decision-making.

My education in relapse prevention and case management has particularly increased my interest in supporting individuals as they work toward healthier choices and greater stability. I understand the importance of meeting people where they are, establishing trust, maintaining appropriate boundaries, recognizing individual strengths, and connecting clients with resources and support systems.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because I want to continue developing my experience within the helping professions while contributing to an environment where adolescents can feel supported, respected, and encouraged to make positive changes. I believe my combination of real-world property management experience, education in substance abuse and case management, and genuine desire to help others would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

I am eager to learn, grow professionally, and bring my strong work ethic, compassion, communication skills, and commitment to helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and career goals could align with your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team and continuing to build my career in the behavioral health and helping-professions field.

Sincerely,

Sondra Garrison

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your mission of helping adolescents and families navigate mental health and substance use treatment immediately stood out to me because it aligns closely with both my professional experience and the work I am passionate about.

In my current role as a Peer Recovery Coach and House Manager with Next Chapter Recovery, I work directly with individuals navigating behavioral health challenges, substance use recovery, and complex life circumstances. Much of my work involves meeting people where they are, listening without judgment, identifying their immediate needs, explaining available resources, and helping them take the next steps toward stability and recovery. I understand that reaching out for help is not always easy, and that the first conversation can make a significant difference in whether someone feels comfortable moving forward.

My background as a Certified Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS), Qualified Behavioral Health Assistant (QBHA), Certified Peer Recovery Coach, and IPS Specialist has strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals and families, navigate behavioral health systems, coordinate services, and advocate for people who may feel overwhelmed by the process. I also have experience connecting individuals with community resources, coordinating with medical and mental health providers, maintaining confidential records, and completing accurate HIPAA-compliant documentation. Having completed the SOAR certification program, I bring additional experience and knowledge related to helping vulnerable populations navigate complex benefits systems.

What I believe I would bring to your admissions team is more than the ability to answer calls and coordinate paperwork. I understand the human side of asking for help. Families reaching out about their adolescent may be frightened, uncertain, or overwhelmed. They need someone who can listen, communicate clearly, remain compassionate, and help turn an overwhelming situation into manageable next steps. I take pride in being dependable, following through, and making sure people do not feel forgotten once they have reached out for support.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and commitment to recovery and behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Angela Kenney, CPFS, QBHA

My professional experience has strengthened my ability to remain calm under pressure, maintain confidentiality, communicate effectively with families and multidisciplinary teams, and manage responsibilities with attention to detail. Above all, I am passionate about making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. I take pride in approaching every individual with dignity, empathy, and respect, recognizing that each person has a unique story and deserves to feel heard and supported.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and compassionate approach could contribute to your admissions team and the families you serve.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. What caught my attention about this opportunity was the chance to help individuals and families during a time when they may need support the most. Mental health is something I genuinely care about, and I believe that sometimes simply having someone listen, show compassion, and help you figure out the next step can make a meaningful difference.

I have over eight years of experience in healthcare administration, education, and customer service. During my time working in a medical office, I handled patient scheduling, insurance verification, referrals, prior authorizations, and electronic medical records. However, one of the most important things I learned was how to communicate with patients who may be frustrated, overwhelmed, or simply looking for answers. I always tried to make sure people felt heard, respected, and comfortable asking questions.

I also earned my bachelor's degree in Psychology, graduating Magna Cum Laude with a 3.79 GPA, and I am currently pursuing my master's degree in Criminal Justice. My education has given me a deeper understanding of human behavior and the importance of mental health, but it has also reinforced something I have always believed: everyone deserves kindness, patience, and access to the support they need.

As a military spouse and mother of three, I understand the importance of being adaptable, organized, and dependable. Moving with my family has taught me how to adjust to change, manage responsibilities, and stay focused even when life gets busy. While I only worked briefly in behavioral health admissions and not directly in a fully remote position, I am comfortable using electronic systems, communicating over the phone, and working independently. I am also not bilingual, but I am always willing to learn and improve my skills.

What I appreciate most about your programs is that you recognize how difficult it can be for someone to reach out for help. I would love the opportunity to be a reassuring voice on the other end of the phone and help individuals and families feel a little less overwhelmed as they begin their journey toward healing.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would truly appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and willingness to learn to your team.

Sincerely,
Christina Harris

Thank you for taking the time to read a bit about me, and my perspective of the work we do. As you can review my resume for details about my work experience and education, please allow me to share about myself, my approach to my work, and the space that I strive to create with my clients. 

To me, nothing is more human than people uniting to support one another, to grow, to heal, and to cultivate vibrant community. In my own life I have been honored to witness and experience the profound impact that empathy, support, and a network of resources can have on someone facing challenges. This has fueled my desire to not only create a safe space for healing for my clinical clients, but also strengthen networks that can serve as a healing net for individuals. We know that systemic barriers can impact individuals’ access to care, support, education, employment, housing, and so many other crucial areas of day to day life. I aim to address these disparities in my work. This is why I am applying to this specific position, and one of the many reasons why I think I will make a great fit for the role. 

Through handling admin in insurance, documenting in various EHRs, case management in a hospital setting, crisis counseling, referral work, clinical work, teaching and tutoring, and so many other opportunities I have had, I have  created a strong and wide foundation of skills and competencies. A main focus of mine has been clinical work thus far in my career, with coordination and administrative work steadily alongside. While I feel a deep connection to the clinical work we do, I am excited to begin a greater shift towards case management, because I absolutely thrive in areas of coordination and organization, and all of the “behind the scenes” work of these roles. 

Those I work with in both clinical and non-clinical contexts have expressed that they feel a unique and genuine sense of empathy, understanding, and empowerment from me. They value my ability to foster an environment where vulnerability is welcomed, appreciating that I emphasize openness and authenticity, as well as the emphasis I place on celebrating progress and successes.

Thank you for taking this time, and for your consideration.  I look forward to hearing from you, and speaking further!

Warmly,
Simone

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My extensive background in remote healthcare communications, behavioral health services, client intake, crisis intervention, and program management has prepared me to excel in this position.

My remote healthcare experience includes working with Always on Call, providing inbound telephone support for DCH Hospital, North Harbor Mental Facility, UMC Mental Center, and Indian Rivers Behavioral Health Clinic. I also worked remotely for two years as an Off-Site Receptionist with Legacy Connections, supporting multiple companies through telephone communications, scheduling, documentation, and customer service. These experiences strengthened my ability to work independently, handle sensitive information, and provide compassionate assistance to callers.

Currently, I serve as Program Manager at The Salvation Army Center of Hope, overseeing operations serving approximately 60 individuals and supervising 10–20 employees. My responsibilities include client intake, assessments, referrals, crisis intervention, confidential documentation, and service coordination. Previously, as a Residential Coordinator and Qualified Developmental Disability Professional with Volunteers of America, I supervised 25–30 employees while coordinating individualized services for approximately 35–40 intellectual clients.

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello, I am a warm, friendly, outgoing people-person — deeply driven by purpose, connection, and helping others grow. Whether in consulting, coaching, education, or managing complex projects, I bring a
people-centered mindset paired with strong execution. I build trust quickly, foster team morale, and deliver results that reflect both heart and strategy.
In 2009, a near-fatal work-related motor vehicle accident changed my life. I lost the ability to read, write, and speak clearly. Recovery demanded resilience — mentally, emotionally, and physically. I enrolled in a Master of Counseling program, rebuilding my capacity while pursuing my lifelong
passion for helping others. Counseling challenged my fear of public speaking and strengthened my ability to guide people through transformation.
Though I valued my time in private practice, I discovered I thrive in team environments — where collaboration, structure, and motivation fuel impact. A personal health journey, including significant weight loss, deepened my understanding of change, discipline, and balance. 

Today, I am thriving — and ready to bring my energy and skills into a role where I can continue to impact the world by helping those around me.

Paul Lindell: The Wellness Architect with a Mission
Builder of trust. Facilitator of hope. I’ve contributed to wellness-centered programs supporting staff resilience and organizational well-being — including Critical Incident Stress Management, the
Peer-to-Peer Trauma Support Team, and volunteer-based initiatives like the Wellness Advocates and Wellness Liaisons. I’ve also helped deliver multiple trainings such as Balance, Blend & Boundaries, Launch Restored, Rediscovering Your Why?, and the Wellness 360 series — all designed to equip staff with tools to sustain wellness in their work and lives.
My background blends communication, coaching, public speaking, and project leadership. I’ve managed high-value accounts, built strong partnerships, and supported teams under pressure —
always with the goal of helping others reach their full potential.

I share my story to connect, not impress. My journey allows me to lead with empathy while executing with clarity and strength. I’d be honored to bring that same commitment to your team.

Warm regards,

Paul Lindell

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a psychology student at the University of Wisconsin–Green Bay with professional experience in behavioral health and supporting children and adolescents with diverse emotional and developmental needs, I am passionate about helping young people and their families access compassionate, effective mental health care.

Through my work as a Behavioral Technician at Trio and my previous experience providing respite care at Celebrate Autism, I have developed strong skills in communication, relationship-building, behavioral support, and responding calmly to challenging situations. These experiences have taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are, listening without judgment, and creating an environment where people feel heard, respected, and supported.

I am currently pursuing my bachelor's degree in psychology, maintaining a 3.8 GPA, with plans to continue my education in clinical mental health or social work. My academic studies in psychopathology, physiological psychology, and human behavior have strengthened my understanding of mental health challenges and reinforced my commitment to working with adolescents and families.

What particularly draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to support families during what may be one of the most difficult and vulnerable moments of their lives. I understand that reaching out for mental health treatment can feel overwhelming, and I believe the first person a family speaks with can make a meaningful difference in their willingness to seek help. I would approach every conversation with empathy, professionalism, patience, and a genuine desire to help families take that important next step.

In addition to my direct care experience, I bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and the ability to communicate effectively with individuals from a wide range of backgrounds. I am comfortable working independently, learning new systems, and balancing multiple responsibilities while maintaining a compassionate, person-centered approach.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission of connecting adolescents and families with the treatment and support they need. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to adolescent mental health could benefit your team.

Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. With over 13 years of experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, mental health services, and case management, I have developed a strong passion for helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances and access the support and resources they need to succeed.

Throughout my career, I have worked with diverse populations, including adults, children, families, and unaccompanied minors. My experience includes crisis intervention, client advocacy, discharge planning, care coordination, resource navigation, and connecting individuals with appropriate treatment and community services. In my current role as a Case Manager at The Haven Detox Arizona, I work closely with clients, clinical teams, healthcare providers, and community organizations to coordinate services and support individuals throughout their recovery journey.

I bring strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills, along with the ability to work with individuals from different backgrounds and circumstances. I understand the importance of meeting people where they are, listening without judgment, and creating an environment where individuals feel heard, supported, and respected.

My educational background includes an Associate Degree in Medical Billing and Coding, a Bachelor's Degree in Psychology, and a Master's Degree in Human Services. Combined with my professional experience, my education has strengthened my understanding of human behavior, mental health, and the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

I am passionate about making a meaningful difference in people's lives. I believe everyone deserves to be heard, supported, and given the opportunity to move forward. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and commitment to helping others to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with your organization's needs.

Sincerely,

Elizabeth Talamante

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over five years of experience in customer service, behavioral health support, administrative assistance, and community outreach, I bring a combination of strong communication skills, compassion, and a genuine passion for helping individuals and families access the support they need.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked in behavioral health settings, providing support to individuals with varying needs, as well as in receptionist and customer service roles where professionalism, patience, organization, and effective communication were essential. My experience working as a behavioral therapist and supporting youth has strengthened my ability to connect with individuals, demonstrate empathy, remain calm in challenging situations, and approach sensitive conversations with understanding and professionalism.

I also bring experience handling administrative responsibilities, assisting clients, answering inquiries, and creating positive first impressions. I understand how important the initial interaction can be, particularly for families seeking mental health or substance use treatment for their children. I would approach every conversation with compassion, attentiveness, and a commitment to making families feel heard, respected, and supported.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it allows me to combine my professional background with my passion for mental health advocacy and helping young people. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team and help families take an important first step toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and dedication would make me a valuable addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Shaina Burns

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines compassionate communication, meaningful client support, and organization in a role where the first interaction can make a lasting difference. I would bring a warm, professional, and dependable approach to helping individuals and families feel heard, supported, and guided toward the care they need.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience, especially for families navigating difficult circumstances. I believe every caller deserves patience, empathy, and clear communication. I would approach each interaction with care while helping callers understand treatment options, coordinating next steps, and ensuring they feel supported throughout the admissions process.

I am highly organized, detail-oriented, and committed to following through on responsibilities. I understand the importance of accurate documentation, timely follow-up, confidentiality, and maintaining clear records. I would take pride in supporting the admissions team by keeping information organized, helping coordinate assessments and intake paperwork, and ensuring each inquiry receives the attention it deserves.

What makes this opportunity especially meaningful to me is the chance to contribute to an organization that helps adolescents and adults take important steps toward healing and recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to represent Adolescent Wellness Academy with professionalism, compassion, and a genuine commitment to making the admissions experience as smooth and reassuring as possible.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to contribute to your team and support your mission of helping individuals and families access meaningful care.

Sincerely,
Mikayla

Dear Hiring Manager,

With a Bachelor’s degree in Guidance and Counseling, professional experience as a Guidance Counselor, and my current role as a Mental Health Technician at Temple University Hospital, I bring a strong foundation in mental health support, crisis intervention, communication, and compassionate client care.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my passion for adolescent mental health with my ability to communicate effectively, coordinate services, and support families navigating challenging circumstances. Orane Hibbert

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in mental health services, clinical work, and program support, I bring a combination of administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills that align well with the responsibilities of this role. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the process of accessing mental health and substance use treatment during what can often be a difficult and overwhelming time.

In my previous role as a Program Support Specialist within Post-Release Services, I developed experience supporting program operations, coordinating services, maintaining documentation, and communicating with individuals and various service providers. This role strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain organized records, facilitate communication, and ensure that important follow-up tasks were completed. Additionally, my clinical experience has provided me with familiarity with electronic health record systems, timely and accurate documentation, client scheduling, and the importance of maintaining confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant practices.

As a mental health professional, I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, patience, and clear communication. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable first step, particularly for adolescents and their families. I would bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental approach to initial inquiries while maintaining the organization, consistency, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process. I am also comfortable navigating conversations that require balancing sensitivity with clear communication, follow-through, and appropriate coordination of services.

Although my background has primarily been in clinical and program support settings rather than a dedicated admissions role, I believe these experiences have equipped me with highly transferable skills. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical perspective, administrative capabilities, and commitment to accessible mental health care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skill set could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Lee-Ferreira

Dear Hiring Manager,
 I am writing to express my interest in the position. I hold a bachelor’s degree in psychology from CUNY Lehman College and bring hands-on experience in case documentation, family engagement, records management, and coordination with multiple stakeholders. I am highly organized, detail-oriented, and committed to supporting students, families, and schools through complex processes. 
In my recent role as a Child Protective Specialist, I managed high volumes of sensitive case information, prepared official documentation, scheduled appointments, and maintained accurate records in compliance with confidentiality requirements. I worked closely with families, internal staff, and external partners to ensure timely communication and proper case handling. This experience closely aligns with the responsibilities of reviewing materials, preparing suspension-related documentation, scheduling hearings, and maintaining accurate databases. 
Previously, as a School Aide, I supported front office operations in a school setting by maintaining attendance records, organizing files, answering phones, directing inquiries, and communicating with families. This role strengthened my understanding of school-based operations, customer service, and collaboration with school personnel. 
Additionally, my long-term experience as a Child Care Provider has enhanced my ability to work effectively with parents and students, explain procedures clearly, and handle sensitive situations with professionalism and empathy. I am comfortable meeting with families both in person and remotely, maintaining ongoing communication, and ensuring that concerns are addressed accurately and respectfully.
 I am proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Google Workspace, and I have strong data entry and records management skills. I am eager to further develop my knowledge of NYCPS systems such as, ATS, and OORS, as well as Chancellor’s Regulations related to student suspensions. I thrive in team-based environments and am committed to providing high-quality technical and administrative support. 
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills can support your team. 
Sincerely, 
Pamela Hernandez

What drew me to this role was the chance to be the first person someone talks to when they’re looking for help. That first call can be hard to make, and I’d want the person on the other end to feel heard and know what to expect next.

At Downtown IMPACT, I spent more than two years supporting clients in a behavioral health setting. I answered a high volume of calls, helped clients understand what services were available, scheduled appointments for two doctors, and checked Medi-Cal eligibility. I also kept confidential client records up to date in SmartCare and R2DB. I learned to explain information clearly and give each person my attention, even when the office was busy.

In my current role at Quietech Associates, I handle intake when clients bring in their computers for service. I listen to what they were doing when the issue started, ask follow-up questions about what they’re seeing, and document the details so the technician knows where to start. I also coordinate appointments, explain what happens next, and follow up when something is still open. That work has taught me how to guide a conversation when someone knows something is wrong but isn’t sure how to explain it.

I’d bring that same patience, attention to detail, and follow-through to helping teens, families, and adults connect with care. Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the chance to talk with you about how my experience could support your admissions team.

Best,
Samantha McGlone
