Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I know how much that first conversation can mean to a family. As a parent who has supported my own teen through mental health challenges, I understand what it feels like to know your child needs help and still have questions about where to begin. I want to be someone a parent or teen feels comfortable asking those questions, especially the ones that are hard to say out loud.

In my current role as a remote Care Coordinator at Cecelia Health, I conduct intake assessments for members entering our weight management program and manage scheduling for our registered dietitians. I speak with members about their needs, document our conversations, schedule appointments, and follow up to keep their care on track. Some members are also navigating mental health challenges, and I’ve learned how important it is to listen at their pace and explain what they can expect next. My previous work at Pediatric Dental Associates also gave me hands-on experience verifying insurance and following up on prior authorizations.

I’ve built my career in customer service because I genuinely care about what happens to the person on the other end of the phone. When someone has a question I can’t answer right away, I take the time to find the information and get back to them. I would bring that same patience and follow-through to each teen, parent, or adult reaching out to your programs.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my intake and scheduling experience, along with my perspective as a parent, could serve your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Brianna Fletcher

I am writing to express my interest in a remote position with your organization. I am a second-year graduate student in Marriage and Family Therapy, having completed all required academic coursework, and am eager to apply the knowledge and interpersonal skills I have developed through my education and professional experience.

My graduate studies have provided me with a strong foundation in several therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Motivational Interviewing, trauma-informed care, mindfulness-based techniques, and substance abuse treatment. My most recent coursework focused on working with adolescents and their families, expanding my understanding of adolescent development, family dynamics, communication challenges, and the importance of providing developmentally appropriate, supportive care.

My interest in substance abuse and its impact on individuals and families is also informed by personal experience with addiction within my own family. In addition to my academic background, I bring a diverse professional history in customer service, food service, management, administration, and property operations. I take pride in being dependable, adaptable, personable, and attentive to the needs of others.

I am particularly interested in opportunities that allow me to combine my educational background and passion for helping others with my established strengths in customer service and administrative support. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I recently applied for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position and wanted to share why this work
matters to me. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, they
may be worried and unsure where to start. I’d like to be the person who listens, explains the next step
clearly, and follows through on what I said I would do.

At True North Pediatrics, I helped families with patient intake, scheduling, referrals, and insurance
verification. I kept patient records up to date and followed up when information was missing. As a
Child Protective Investigator with the Florida Department of Children and Families, I spoke with
children and caregivers during difficult circumstances and documented sensitive information with
care. Both roles taught me how much it matters to stay calm, ask clear questions, and make sure
families know what happens next.
I’m fluent in English and Spanish, and I’ve supported clients by phone, email, and video. My studies in
forensic psychology and my training as a Christian Mental Health Coach have deepened my interest in
how families navigate the decision to seek help.

I’d bring that perspective to your admissions team along with the practical habits I’ve built in pediatric care: keeping track of referrals, protecting confidential information, and following up when a family is waiting for an answer.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Lizmar Encarnacion-Rosario

Dear Hiring Manager,

I would love the opportunity to introduce myself as I begin planning the next chapter of my life and career. After spending the past several years living and working in Springfield, Missouri, I am exploring a return to the Mt. Vernon, Illinois area. Southern Illinois has always felt like home, and I welcome opportunities that could help me make that move while bringing me closer to my family.

Throughout my career, I have found that my greatest strength and passion is working with people. Whether I am helping someone navigate a difficult situation, answering questions, solving problems, or simply making someone’s day a little easier, I genuinely enjoy being the person others can count on. I believe that kindness, patience, and a willingness to help can make a difference in just about any workplace.

My professional experience has given me a strong background in administrative support, office coordination, healthcare services, and customer relations. In my current position as Intake Coordinator with Synergy Counseling Center, I help manage the daily operations of a busy outpatient mental health and substance abuse treatment facility. My responsibilities include scheduling for approximately 15 therapists, insurance verification, confidential records management, payment processing, and providing administrative assistance to both clients and clinical staff.

Over the years, I have learned the importance of being organized, dependable, adaptable, and able to handle multiple responsibilities while maintaining a welcoming and professional environment. I take pride in being someone who can step in, find solutions, and help things run a little more smoothly.

While much of my experience has been in healthcare and behavioral health, I am certainly not limiting myself to those fields. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my administrative experience, strong work ethic, and genuine love of helping people to an organization where I can make a positive contribution.

As I consider relocating to the Mt. Vernon, Illinois area, I am reaching out to make professional connections and explore opportunities with organizations that may be a good fit, whenever the timing is right for both of us.

Thank you for taking the time to learn a little about me. I would truly appreciate the opportunity to speak with you and learn more about your organization. I look forward to the possibility of becoming part of a team where I can contribute, continue learning, and make a difference.

Warm regards,

Darla Kay Oliver

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. My experience across different age groups and care settings has given me a broad perspective, adaptability, and a strong understanding of the importance of individualized support. I am comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities, collaborating with colleagues, and recognizing the importance of both efficient administrative processes and meaningful human connection.

Thank you for considering my application. Warm regards,

Jorge Ruiz

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy . Being the first voice someone hears on a hard day is work I take seriously, and I have spent most of my career as the first point of contact for people who need help, answers, and a clear next step.
As Lead Concierge at Inspired Living (Validus Senior Living), I answered multi-line phones, greeted residents and families, resolved their requests, and routed issues to the right department. I coordinated schedules and updates between departments and outside vendors, and I tracked and closed work orders across two software platforms. As a Call Screener, I screened prospective clients by phone and scheduled 20-30 appointments a day, confirming each one to reduce no-shows, which is the same follow-through this role depends on. As a remote Sales Representative at Comcast, I handled inbound customer calls from home, explained plans and services in plain language, and documented every interaction accurately. As a Nursing Assistant at Woodland Grove Health and Rehabilitation, I provided daily personal care, recorded care activities in resident charts, and learned to work with sensitive information in a healthcare setting.
Since 2024 I have worked for myself and managed my own schedule and projects without daily direction, including running a small print-on-demand shop. I am calm, patient, and a good listener, and I keep careful records. I care deeply about giving supporting mental health struggles and substance abuse issues as someone who suffered without a solid support system in my youth. I would love to give back to the community.
I want to be direct: I have not worked in behavioral health admissions, and I have not used Kipu or done insurance verification. I am a fast learner who already works comfortably in account, scheduling, and tracking systems, and I would put the same care into learning your processes and keeping every lead followed up until the person is scheduled or connected to the right place.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your callers and your team.
Sincerely,
Alexandra Hernandez

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. This role resonates with me personally. I have my own experience with mental health treatment, so I know how hard it can be to reach out for help, and I understand how much it matters that the first voice someone hears is calm, kind, and clear about what comes next. That is the kind of voice I want to be for your callers and their families.
I am a Certified Nursing Assistant at Turlock Nursing and Rehab, where I work directly with residents and their care teams every day. I chart in PointClickCare, report changes in condition to nurses, and follow strict privacy and safety procedures. Being accurate with patient information and respectful of confidentiality is part of my daily routine. I am newer to behavioral health admissions, but I bring real patient care experience, strong documentation habits, and a genuine desire to learn your intake process well.
I have also worked remotely since 2020 as Creative Director for Zanterite, where I manage my own projects and deadlines without daily direction. I use tools like Slack, Trello, and Google Workspace to stay organized and follow through, which I know matters when every caller needs to be scheduled or referred to the right place. Before that, my customer service work at Lowe's and my time as an Assistant Manager at Dollar General taught me to stay patient with people who are stressed, listen closely, and keep service consistent.
I am fluent in English and Spanish, and I would be glad to help Spanish-speaking callers and families feel comfortable during a difficult time. I learn new systems quickly, and I would welcome the chance to learn Kipu and your insurance verification process.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would love to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families you serve.
Sincerely,
Stephanie Valdizon

With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, experience in behavioral health case management, and fluency in English and Spanish, I would bring compassionate communication, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to helping families access care.

This work requires accurate documentation, attention to confidentiality, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while remaining responsive to each family’s needs.

I have experience supporting adolescents and caregivers navigating depression, anxiety, trauma, behavioral challenges, and psychiatric hospitalizations. I understand how overwhelming seeking treatment can feel, and I approach families with patience, empathy, and clear explanations. My bilingual skills also allow me to communicate directly with Spanish-speaking families and help reduce language barriers.

I am eager to bring these transferable skills to admissions, helping families understand next steps, coordinating with clinical teams, and supporting a timely transition into appropriate treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team and help adolescents and their families feel supported from their first contact.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my experience and dedication to accessible behavioral health care align with this position.

Sincerely,
Ledy Martinez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Social Work, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, case management, and substance use support, I bring a combination of clinical understanding, administrative coordination, and compassionate communication. As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am especially passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to accessing mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. I understand the importance of maintaining confidentiality, accurate documentation, and consistent communication when coordinating behavioral health services remotely.

Additionally, as a Bilingual Parent Support Specialist at Catholic Charities' Guadalupe Home, I support young mothers experiencing various challenges, including substance use concerns, in a residential shelter environment. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I understand that individuals and families seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or afraid. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background can support your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Jennyfer Alvidrez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m interested in the intake role because I know what it can take to make that first call. I’ve been the person calling for help for myself, and I’ve been the daughter of the desperate parent on the phone trying to find help. I remember how hard it was to explain what was happening while trying to understand what kind of help was available. I’d bring that perspective to every conversation with a teen or family reaching out to your program.

I’m a survivor of human trafficking, and my own recovery included residential treatment, outpatient care, and peer support. Those experiences taught me how much it matters to be heard without judgment and to leave a conversation knowing what comes next. I would give teens room to speak for themselves, listen to what their families are worried about, and explain the next steps in plain language. Every caller’s circumstances are different, and I would let them tell me what they need in their own words.

My professional background also prepares me for the day-to-day work of intake. I’ve spent years working with children and families as a nanny and household manager, including supporting children with special needs. In my administrative roles, I learned to ask clear questions, keep accurate records, handle private information with discretion, and follow through when several things needed attention at once. I’m comfortable staying calm when someone is overwhelmed and making sure the details they share reach the right person.

I’d welcome the chance to be the person who picks up the phone, helps a family feel heard, and makes the next step easier to take. Thank you for considering my application.

Lea Jones

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to have the opportunity to apply to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your mission to create a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment for adolescents facing mental health challenges aligns closely with my values, education, and experience. I am passionate about helping others feel seen, heard, and valued, and I welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team making a meaningful difference in young people's lives.

I hold a bachelor's degree in Psychology with a minor in Family Science and am currently pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. I have four years of experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, providing one-on-one support to children and adolescents up to age 18 on the autism spectrum in home and clinical settings. In this role, I implemented evidence-based interventions, monitored client progress through data collection, and maintained a safe, supportive environment. As an Intervention Specialist, I also supported elementary-aged students with their academic, behavioral, and individual needs.

Beyond my direct experience working with children, I have developed strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills. In my role leading volunteer operations for my church, I had the privilege of training and supervising more than 30 volunteers a day, ranging in age from 18 to 98. Working with such a diverse group taught me the importance of humility, adaptability, active listening, and recognizing different learning styles. I worked to create an inclusive environment where every individual felt heard and valued while helping improve daily operations through collaboration and individualized training. I also provided administrative support by answering phones, assisting visitors, responding to questions, and coordinating schedules.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to connection, compassion, and individualized care. I believe one of the most meaningful things we can offer is a place where individuals feel safe to be themselves and know they are not alone and that they have value and purpose. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the chance to join your team and support the important work you do.

Sincerely, Kaley Rhoton

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Specialized Associate’s Degree in Medical Assisting, extensive experience in healthcare administration and patient coordination, and over 15 years of customer service experience, I believe I bring a strong combination of medical knowledge, communication skills, and compassion that would make me an asset to your admissions team.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have worked in several specialty settings, including pain management, and wellness. My experience includes coordinating patient appointments and referrals, communicating with patients and providers, maintaining electronic medical records, handling confidential health information, and helping patients navigate the next steps in their care. I am familiar with EMR systems, Athena, medical terminology, HIPAA compliance, and the importance of accurate documentation and timely follow-up.

I understand that the admissions process is often someone’s first interaction with a healthcare organization, and that first impression matters. My background in both healthcare and customer service has taught me how to actively listen, establish trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and communicate information in a way that makes people feel comfortable and understood. My caregiving experience has further strengthened my patience, compassion, and ability to support individuals and families through challenging circumstances.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the meaningful work your programs provide to adolescents and adults seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, both for individuals and their loved ones. I would take that responsibility seriously by approaching every inquiry with empathy, professionalism, discretion, and a commitment to helping each caller find an appropriate next step.

I am organized, adaptable, self-motivated, and comfortable managing multiple responsibilities in fast paced environments. I understand the importance of maintaining accurate lead records, following up consistently, coordinating documentation, and ensuring that no inquiry falls through the cracks. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and processes quickly while maintaining a high standard of patient communication and organization.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare background, administrative experience, and genuine passion for helping others to your growing team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my qualifications could contribute to your admissions department.

Sincerely,

Christine Cushley

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. I have worked with a few of you closely already! As a licensed therapist with over 10 years of experience in behavioral healthcare, including serving as Director of Admissions at Galen Hope, I bring a unique combination of clinical expertise, operational leadership, and a genuine passion for improving access to quality mental health treatment.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with adolescents and families navigating complex mental health challenges, including anxiety, depression, eating disorders, and co-occurring conditions. As a licensed clinician, I understand the importance of evidence-based treatment, family involvement, and individualized care, particularly during the critical developmental years of adolescence.

In my previous leadership role, I oversaw admissions operations, led and trained teams, streamlined workflows, monitored performance metrics, and collaborated closely with clinical, administrative, and business development departments. My experience navigating levels of care, including PHP and IOP, has given me a strong understanding of the clinical and operational considerations necessary to deliver effective treatment while maintaining high standards of patient care.

What particularly excites me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my clinical background with my strengths in leadership, program development, and operational strategy. I understand that a successful virtual IOP requires more than strong clinical programming; it requires an engaged team, efficient systems, meaningful family collaboration, and an environment where adolescents feel supported and connected, even through a screen.

I pride myself on being an approachable, collaborative, and solutions-oriented leader who values both clinical excellence and the people responsible for delivering it. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, energy, and commitment to adolescent mental health to AWA, helping strengthen and grow a program that makes meaningful treatment accessible to more families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and leadership approach align with AWA's mission.

Warm regards,

Chloe Godward

To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Psychology graduate, I have been looking for an opportunity to work in a mental health setting where I can contribute to something meaningful while continuing to develop professionally. I enjoy remote work and the organization and communication that come with it, but what matters most to me is knowing that my work is helping people.

My interest in this field has grown even stronger since beginning my volunteer experience with the Alachua Crisis Center. It has reminded me how important it is to have people who are willing to listen, offer support, and help others through difficult moments. It has also made me realize how much I want my everyday work to be connected to making a difference in someone's life.

I previously worked at Nicaragua Recovery, a residential recovery program, where I supported patients through daily check-ins, activities, and recovery programming. I facilitated daily One Day at a Time reflection groups and translated the discussions into English for patients who did not speak Spanish so they could participate fully. I also interpreted conversations between patients and their outside caregivers, helping make communication easier and ensuring patients could better understand and express themselves. Later, I worked remotely as an Outreach Coordinator for the same program, contacting prospective patients, explaining the program, answering questions, and communicating with clinics and therapists about potential referrals.

In my current remote administrative position, I manage correspondence, organize information, communicate with customers, and coordinate with different departments. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to stay organized, communicate clearly, and manage tasks independently. I would be excited to bring these skills into a mental health setting where the administrative work directly supports patients, families, and clinical teams.

As a native English and Spanish speaker with a degree in Psychology, I would value the opportunity to contribute to AWA's work with adolescents and their families. I am dependable, eager to learn, and genuinely motivated to build a career in a field where I can help others.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and motivation could contribute to your team.

My approach to art is centered on the process rather than the final product; I believe the arts should be an opportunity to experiment, take risks, make mistakes, and express yourself without the pressure of getting something "right." My previous experience as an ABA Teacher has also taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are and creating supportive environments where everyone feels welcome to participate.

My creative background extends beyond visual art to include writing, music, and theatre. These experiences have deepened my appreciation for the many ways people communicate and express themselves, and I'm drawn to opportunities that allow others to explore those possibilities.

My connection to art is also personal. Throughout my own experiences, creativity has been a meaningful way to process and make sense of my emotions. I've come to appreciate the value of having the space to process without judgement or expectations. This is an environment I hope to foster for others; one where individuals feel safe to explore their emotions, connect with each other, and perhaps even learn something new about themselves along the way.

I would be grateful for the chance to contribute my creativity and enthusiasm for the therapeutic arts to the AWA community. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,
Charity Ortiz, BA, RBT

Sincerely,

 Anna Babinchak
